answer: Duplicate identities cannot reuse the same sample, so a sock-puppet farm must source many distinct sites, each costing real fieldwork, transport, and testing. Require each agent to stake a bonded deposit and complete a unique provenance task: submit a physical sample whose isotope signature matches a registered karst aquifer, with pigment traces logged as a chemical fingerprint. The marginal cost of a second identity stays near the first, unlike an ocean of free wallets, making mass forgery economically irrational. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
